file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
(`Authorization: Bearer` works too). Send a User-Agent of your own: the edge in
front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.

## LLM calls

Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.

The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:

```
$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
```

`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:

| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |

The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.

### Your key

Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.

With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
as `x-api-key`:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
```

A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:

```python
import os
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
    http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
```

```javascript
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"

const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
  httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
```

A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.

**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
`401`.

A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
context.

### How cost is measured

Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
A model too new for the platform's price list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it, its long-context price
included. An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.

The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.

### Team secrets

Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:

```sh
curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
```

Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
cannot be platform variables (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_SERVER_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`,
`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `PATH`, `HOME`, `DISPLAY`, …). A team keeps at most 20; each value is 16 characters to 4 KB long.

## Scored run

Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
[Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
`127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:

- **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
- **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
  and the websites.
- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.

1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
   to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your

# FAQ and event details

## FAQ

**Which models can I use?** The hosted models are free, and the starter kit shows how to call them. Or bring your own key for
any provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, or others the
organizers add) and send its calls through the metering proxy. `GET /v1/runs/current` lists the proxy base URLs. Models must have a published
price (a model too new for the platform's list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it; OpenRouter reports its own)
and satisfy any organizer model allowlist. See
[the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) for SDK setup.

**Where do I keep my model key?** As a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets): the team page's Secrets list
injects it into your agent's run step in test and scored runs, redacted from logs. Don't put keys in your
package; we store packages and the review agent reads them.

**Why does my model call get a 401?** "Add your OpenAI API key to the request" means no provider key arrived: set
`OPENAI_API_KEY` (in test and scored runs, as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets)). A 401 from the
provider itself means the key is wrong. Check that `OPENAI_BASE_URL` points at the run's proxy
(`$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1`, already set in test and scored runs); the same holds for any OpenAI-compatible provider.

and approves it in the browser. Every device gets its own token; there is no shared team key to pass around.

**I lost a laptop, or a token leaked.** Revoke that device's token on your team page under Signed-in devices
(`atira logout` revokes the one on the computer you are at). Leaving or being removed from a team ends your
tokens' access to it at once.

the captain invited, or ask the captain to invite your GitHub username.

**Does it cost me anything?** We charge nothing, and the models the platform hosts are free and never charged. If
you bring your own key for another provider, that provider bills your key. The proxy measures every call and

scouting logins), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run ./my-agent`). A test run runs on `public-1`, the public

counts: a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.

## LLM calls

Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.

The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:

```
$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
```

`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:

| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |

The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.

### Your key

Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.

With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
as `x-api-key`:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
```

A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:

```python
import os
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
    http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
```

```javascript
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"

const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
  httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
```

A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.

**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
`401`.

A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
context.

### How cost is measured

Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
A model too new for the platform's price list counts at the price OpenRouter lists for it, its long-context price
included. An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.

The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.

### Team secrets

Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:

```sh
curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
```

Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
cannot be platform variables (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_SERVER_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`,
`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `PATH`, `HOME`, `DISPLAY`, …). A team keeps at most 20; each value is 16 characters to 4 KB long.

## Scored run

Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run

- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
  and the websites.
- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.

content.content:
"""
The model behind the workers: the hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy by default.

AGENT_MODEL picks another model on the same OpenAI-compatible endpoint (QWEN_BASE_URL). Thinking is off for
navigation steps, which makes a step about three times faster, and on where a worker has to weigh evidence.

Timeouts are per mode, because the hosted model now and then hangs a call for minutes until the proxy drops it: a
thinking-off step answers in 2 to 5 s, so it gets a short timeout and a quick retry (LLM_TIMEOUT, 45 s, which
leaves room for the 30 to 36 s calls a longer answer takes); a thinking-on call legitimately takes 25 to 45 s, so it
gets a long one (LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING, 90 s). Time grows with the answer: copying 80 table rows took 85 s even
without thinking. `settings(thinking)` carries the right timeout in the ModelSettings; pydantic-ai passes it to
the OpenAI client per request, so one client serves both modes. A call known to run longer (a reader writing a long
typed answer) passes `settings(thinking, timeout=seconds)`; that per-request value beats any timeout set on the
client. LLM_RETRIES attempts follow each failure with a short backoff (0.5 s doubling, capped at 8 s).

The timeout bounds the whole call, not each read: while the model works, the proxy sends the headers and then a
newline every few seconds, so a plain read timeout never fires and a hung call would run until the proxy gives up.

LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1 swaps the whole-call deadline for progress checks (see `_WatchdogModel`): each call is
streamed, a call whose first chunk does not arrive within LLM_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT (20 s) is retried, and a call
that is answering may run on as long as it keeps making progress, up to LLM_MAX_CALL (300 s). The proxy streams
text and reasoning token by token but holds back tool-call arguments until they are complete, so a request with
tools may stay silent after its last token for as long as its timeout above; one without tools may pause
LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT (15 s). LLM_HEDGE_AFTER sends a second copy of a call that has not started after that many
seconds and keeps whichever starts first (the losing copy may still be billed).
"""
import asyncio
import contextvars
import os
import time
from contextlib import AsyncExitStack

import httpx2
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelAPIError, ModelHTTPError
from pydantic_ai.messages import ModelMessage, ModelResponse
from pydantic_ai.models import ModelRequestParameters
from pydantic_ai.models.openai import OpenAIChatModel
from pydantic_ai.providers.openai import OpenAIProvider
from pydantic_ai.settings import ModelSettings

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 45.0  # thinking off: steps answer in seconds, so a hang shows early
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_THINKING = 90.0  # thinking on: a call reading a whole page may take 25 to 45 s
DEFAULT_RETRIES = 6
os.environ.setdefault("PYDANTIC_AI_NO_BANNER", "1")


def env_seconds(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    """A positive number from the environment, or `default` when unset, empty or unusable."""
    try:
        value = float(os.environ.get(name, "") or default)
    except ValueError:
        return default
    return value if value > 0 else default


def timeout_seconds(thinking: bool = False) -> float:
    """Seconds one model call may take before it is given up and retried: LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING for thinking-on
    calls (falling back to LLM_TIMEOUT when it is larger), LLM_TIMEOUT otherwise."""
    short = env_seconds("LLM_TIMEOUT", DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
    if not thinking:
        return short
    return max(short, env_seconds("LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING", DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_THINKING))


def retries() -> int:
    """How many times a failed or timed-out call is retried (LLM_RETRIES, default 6; 0 turns retries off)."""
    try:
        value = int(os.environ.get("LLM_RETRIES", "") or DEFAULT_RETRIES)
    except ValueError:
        return DEFAULT_RETRIES
    return value if value >= 0 else DEFAULT_RETRIES


DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN = 20.0  # measured: the first chunk came within 9.4 s (p90 5.9 s) in 179 calls, either mode
DEFAULT_IDLE = 15.0  # text and reasoning tokens arrive at most ~1.5 s apart while the model answers
DEFAULT_MAX_CALL = 300.0  # a streamed answer is not cut by the proxy: one runaway reasoning ran 814 s


def watchdog() -> bool:
    """Whether calls are streamed and judged by progress (LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1) instead of a whole-call deadline."""
    return os.environ.get("LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG", "").strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")


def hedge_seconds() -> float:
    """After how many seconds without a first chunk a second copy of the call is sent (LLM_HEDGE_AFTER; 0 = never)."""
    try:
        value = float(os.environ.get("LLM_HEDGE_AFTER", "") or 0)
    except ValueError:
        return 0.0
    return max(value, 0.0)


def _backoff(attempt: int) -> float:
    """Seconds to wait before retry `attempt`: 0.5 s doubling, capped at 8 s (as the OpenAI client does)."""
    return min(0.5 * 2 ** (attempt - 1), 8.0)


class Stalled(Exception):
    """A streamed call stopped making progress (raised by the watchdog, then retried)."""


# The progress limits of the call being made in this task; set by _WatchdogModel, read by the stream wrapper.
_WATCH: contextvars.ContextVar["_Limits | None"] = contextvars.ContextVar("llm_watch", default=None)


class _Limits:
    def __init__(self, *, first: float, idle: float, silence: float, tools: bool) -> None:
        self.first, self.idle, self.silence, self.tools = first, idle, silence, tools

    @property
    def quiet(self) -> float:
        """How long the call may go without a token once it has started: a request with tools may be writing tool
        arguments, which the proxy only sends when they are complete."""
        return max(self.idle, self.silence) if self.tools else self.idle


def _progress(chunk) -> bool:
    """Whether a stream chunk carries model output (text, reasoning or a tool call), not just a role or usage."""
    for choice in getattr(chunk, "choices", None) or ():
        delta = choice.delta
        if delta is None:
            continue
        extra = delta.model_extra or {}
        if delta.content or delta.tool_calls or extra.get("reasoning_content") or extra.get("reasoning"):
            return True
    return False


class _WatchedStream:
    """An OpenAI chunk stream that raises Stalled when the call goes quiet for longer than its limits allow.
    The proxy's keep-alive comments never reach here (the SSE decoder drops them), so they do not count."""

    def __init__(self, stream, limits: _Limits) -> None:
        self._stream, self._limits = stream, limits
        self._chunks = 0
        self._last = time.monotonic()

    def _wait(self) -> float:
        quiet = self._limits.first if not self._chunks else self._limits.quiet
        return max(self._last + quiet - time.monotonic(), 0.0)

    async def __aiter__(self):
        source = self._stream.__aiter__()
        while True:
            try:
                chunk = await asyncio.wait_for(anext(source), self._wait())
            except StopAsyncIteration:
                return
            except TimeoutError:
                if not self._chunks:
                    raise Stalled(f"no first chunk within {self._limits.first:g}s") from None
                raise Stalled(f"no progress for {self._limits.quiet:g}s after {self._chunks} chunks") from None
            if not self._chunks or _progress(chunk):
                self._last = time.monotonic()
            self._chunks += 1
            yield chunk

    async def __aenter__(self):
        await self._stream.__aenter__()
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc) -> None:
        await self._stream.__aexit__(*exc)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._stream.close()

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return getattr(self._stream, name)


class _WatchdogModel(OpenAIChatModel):
    """The OpenAI chat model; with LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG on, a request is streamed under progress limits, retried when
    it stalls, and handed back as one ModelResponse, so agents run unchanged."""

    async def _completions_create(self, messages, stream, model_settings, model_request_parameters):
        response = await super()._completions_create(messages, stream, model_settings, model_request_parameters)
        limits = _WATCH.get()
        if stream and limits is not None and not isinstance(response, ModelResponse):
            return _WatchedStream(response, limits)
        return response

    async def request(self, messages: list[ModelMessage], model_settings: ModelSettings | None,
                      model_request_parameters: ModelRequestParameters) -> ModelResponse:
        if not watchdog():
            return await super().request(messages, model_settings, model_request_parameters)
        settings = ModelSettings(**(model_settings or {}))
        thinking = bool(((settings.get("extra_body") or {}).get("chat_template_kwargs") or {}).get("enable_thinking"))
        silence = float(settings.get("timeout") or timeout_seconds(thinking))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        cap = env_seconds("LLM_MAX_CALL", DEFAULT_MAX_CALL)
        settings["timeout"] = cap  # the HTTP layer only guards the cap; progress is judged here
        tools = bool(model_request_parameters.function_tools or model_request_parameters.output_tools)
        limits = _Limits(first=env_seconds("LLM_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT", DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN),
                         idle=env_seconds("LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT", DEFAULT_IDLE), silence=silence, tools=tools)
        attempts = retries() + 1
        for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
            token = _WATCH.set(limits)
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(cap):
                    return await self._attempt(messages, settings, model_request_parameters, limits)
            except (Stalled, TimeoutError, httpx2.TransportError) as error:
                reason = str(error) or f"no answer within {cap:g}s"
            except ModelAPIError as error:
                if isinstance(error, ModelHTTPError) and error.status_code < 500 and error.status_code != 429:
                    raise
                reason = str(error)
            finally:
                _WATCH.reset(token)
            if attempt == attempts:
                raise ModelAPIError(self.model_name, f"model call failed {attempts} times; last: {reason}")
            print(f"[model] stalled thinking {'on' if thinking else 'off'}: {reason}; retry {attempt}/{attempts - 1}",
                  flush=True)
            await asyncio.sleep(_backoff(attempt))
        raise AssertionError("unreachable")

    async def _attempt(self, messages, settings, params, limits: _Limits) -> ModelResponse:
        """One streamed call (two when hedging): wait for the first chunk, then read the stream to its end."""
        async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
            streamed = await self._start(stack, messages, settings, params, limits)
            async for _ in streamed:
                pass
            return streamed.get()

    async def _open(self, messages, settings, params):
        stack = AsyncExitStack()
        try:
            streamed = await stack.enter_async_context(self.request_stream(messages, settings, params))
        except BaseException:
            await stack.aclose()
            raise
        return stack, streamed

    async def _start(self, stack: AsyncExitStack, messages, settings, params, limits: _Limits):
        """Open the stream (request_stream returns once the first chunk is in). With LLM_HEDGE_AFTER, a second copy
        goes out when the first has not started by then; the first copy to start wins, the other is dropped."""
        hedge = hedge_seconds()
        tasks = [asyncio.create_task(self._open(messages, settings, params))]
        first_copy = tasks[0]
        deadline = time.monotonic() + limits.first
        hedged = False
        try:
            if 0 < hedge < limits.first:
                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=hedge)
                if not done:
                    print(f"[model] no first chunk after {hedge:g}s: sending a hedge copy", flush=True)
                    tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._open(messages, settings, params)))
                    deadline = time.monotonic() + limits.first
                    hedged = True
            while tasks:
                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0),
                                             return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
                if not done:
                    raise Stalled(f"no first chunk within {limits.first:g}s")
                for task in done:
                    tasks.remove(task)
                    if task.exception() is None:
                        inner, streamed = task.result()
                        stack.push_async_callback(inner.aclose)
                        if hedged:
                            print(f"[model] hedge: the {'first' if task is first_copy else 'hedge'} copy "
                                  "started first and is kept", flush=True)
                        return streamed
                    if not tasks:
                        raise task.exception()  # type: ignore[misc]
            raise AssertionError("unreachable")
        finally:
            for task in tasks:  # copies that lost the race or never started
                task.cancel()
            for result in await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True):
                if isinstance(result, tuple):
                    await result[0].aclose()


def _thinking(request: httpx2.Request) -> str:
    content = request.content or b""
    return "on" if b'"enable_thinking": true' in content or b'"enable_thinking":true' in content else "off"


async def _sent(request: httpx2.Request) -> None:
    """Note when a call left; a retry (the OpenAI client counts them in a header) is logged, with the timeout the
    attempt runs under, so a hanging model shows in the run logs before the worker times out."""
    request.extensions["sent_at"] = time.monotonic()
    attempt = int(request.headers.get("x-stainless-retry-count", "0") or 0)
    if attempt:
        print(f"[model] retry {attempt}/{retries()} thinking {_thinking(request)} "
              f"timeout {request.headers.get('x-stainless-read-timeout', '?')}s", flush=True)


class _TimedBody(httpx2.AsyncByteStream):
    """A response body that logs the call once it has fully arrived: the proxy sends the headers early and a
    thinking-on body can follow much later, so logging at the headers would hide the real duration."""

    def __init__(self, response: httpx2.Response) -> None:
        self._response = response
        self._stream = response.stream

    @property
    def elapsed(self):
        return getattr(self._stream, "elapsed", None)

    async def __aiter__(self):
        complete = False
        try:
            async for chunk in self._stream:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
                complete = complete or b"data: [DONE]" in chunk  # a stream's reader may stop right there
                yield chunk
            complete = True
        finally:
            _log(self._response, complete)

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        await self._stream.aclose()  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def _log(response: httpx2.Response, complete: bool) -> None:
    """One line per model call: status, seconds until the body was in (and until the headers came), request
    size, thinking mode, and which retry it was."""
    request = response.request
    now = time.monotonic()
    sent, headers = request.extensions.get("sent_at", now), request.extensions.get("headers_at", now)
    attempt = request.headers.get("x-stainless-retry-count", "0")
    print(f"[model] {response.status_code} {now - sent:.1f}s (headers {headers - sent:.1f}s) "
          f"{len(request.content or b'')} bytes thinking {_thinking(request)}"
          + (f" retry {attempt}" if attempt not in ("", "0") else "") + ("" if complete else " incomplete"),
          flush=True)


async def _answered(response: httpx2.Response) -> None:
    """Called when the headers are in: remember when, and log the call once the body has been read."""
    response.request.extensions["headers_at"] = time.monotonic()
    response.stream = _TimedBody(response)


class _DeadlineClient(httpx2.AsyncClient):
    """An HTTP client whose read timeout is a deadline for the whole call (headers and body), so the proxy's
    keep-alive newlines cannot hold a call open past it. Expiry raises ReadTimeout, which the OpenAI client retries."""

    async def send(self, request: httpx2.Request, *, stream: bool = False, **kwargs) -> httpx2.Response:
        seconds = (request.extensions.get("timeout") or {}).get("read")
        if not seconds:
            return await super().send(request, stream=stream, **kwargs)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
        try:
            response = await asyncio.wait_for(super().send(request, stream=True, **kwargs), seconds)
        except TimeoutError:
            raise httpx2.ReadTimeout(f"no answer within {seconds:g}s", request=request) from None
        if stream:
            return response
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(response.aread(), max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.001))
        except TimeoutError:
            await response.aclose()
            raise httpx2.ReadTimeout(f"no complete answer within {seconds:g}s", request=request) from None
        except BaseException:
            await response.aclose()
            raise
        return response


def model() -> OpenAIChatModel:
    """The worker model. The client's own timeout is the thinking-off one; `settings()` overrides it per request,
    so a thinking-on agent gets its longer timeout without a client of its own. With LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG on, the
    model streams each call and judges it by progress instead (`_WatchdogModel`)."""
    client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
                         timeout=timeout_seconds(thinking=False), max_retries=retries(),
                         http_client=_DeadlineClient(event_hooks={"request": [_sent], "response": [_answered]}))
    return _WatchdogModel(os.environ.get("AGENT_MODEL", QWEN_MODEL), provider=OpenAIProvider(openai_client=client))


def thinking(phase: str, default: bool) -> bool:
    """Whether `phase` (BRIEF, FORM, REVIEW, ...) thinks: THINKING_<PHASE>=0/1 overrides the default, so
    experiments can switch it per phase and the run records say which way it ran."""
    value = os.environ.get(f"THINKING_{phase.upper()}", "").strip().lower()
    return default if not value else value not in ("0", "false", "no", "off")


def settings(thinking: bool = False, *, timeout: float | None = None) -> ModelSettings:
    """Model settings for one agent: thinking on or off, and the matching per-request timeout (an explicit
    `timeout` in seconds wins, for calls that are known to be slow or quick regardless of mode)."""
    return ModelSettings(
        temperature=0.2,
        parallel_tool_calls=False,  # one tab per worker: actions must run in order
        timeout=timeout if timeout is not None else timeout_seconds(thinking),
        extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": thinking}},
    )
"""The free hosted models in short: one call each. Docs: $API/start#models and $API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls

Qwen (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): an OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls, images and a 256k context. Every run gets
QWEN_BASE_URL and QWEN_API_KEY; on your machine `atira scout --env` points them at `atira models proxy`, which you
keep running in another terminal.

Clef (Cloudflare Clef): a decision model. POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide with a `state`, up to 4 `images` and your
`questions`: "choice" picks one of your options, "noul" gives the probability of yes, "score" rates on your scale.
CLEF_BASE_URL and CLEF_API_KEY are set only where the platform hosts Clef. A run waits only for the models listed in
agent.json "models" to warm up: list ["qwen", "clef"] if your agent relies on Clef.

Any other provider works with your own key, through the run's metering proxy: see the docs above.
"""
import os

import httpx2 as httpx  # comes with the OpenAI SDK
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def qwen() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    """A client for the hosted Qwen; a cold model takes a while to answer its first call, hence the long timeout."""
    return AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"], timeout=360)


async def ask_qwen(prompt: str) -> str:
    """One chat call: the reply's text."""
    reply = await qwen().chat.completions.create(model=QWEN_MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    return reply.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def ask_clef(state, question: str) -> float:
    """One decision: how likely Clef finds the answer to a yes/no question about `state` (text or JSON) is yes."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120) as client:
        response = await client.post(os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide", json=body,
                                     headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"})
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()["answers"]["q"]["noul"]

"""
The model behind the workers: the hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy by default.

AGENT_MODEL picks another model on the same OpenAI-compatible endpoint (QWEN_BASE_URL). Thinking is off for
navigation steps, which makes a step about three times faster, and on where a worker has to weigh evidence.

Timeouts are per mode, because the hosted model now and then hangs a call for minutes until the proxy drops it: a
thinking-off step answers in 2 to 5 s, so it gets a short timeout and a quick retry (LLM_TIMEOUT, 45 s, which
leaves room for the 30 to 36 s calls a longer answer takes); a thinking-on call legitimately takes 25 to 45 s, so it
gets a long one (LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING, 90 s). Time grows with the answer: copying 80 table rows took 85 s even
without thinking. `settings(thinking)` carries the right timeout in the ModelSettings; pydantic-ai passes it to
the OpenAI client per request, so one client serves both modes. A call known to run longer (a reader writing a long
typed answer) passes `settings(thinking, timeout=seconds)`; that per-request value beats any timeout set on the
client. LLM_RETRIES attempts follow each failure with a short backoff (0.5 s doubling, capped at 8 s).

The timeout bounds the whole call, not each read: while the model works, the proxy sends the headers and then a
newline every few seconds, so a plain read timeout never fires and a hung call would run until the proxy gives up.

LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1 swaps the whole-call deadline for progress checks (see `_WatchdogModel`): each call is
streamed, a call whose first chunk does not arrive within LLM_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT (20 s) is retried, and a call
that is answering may run on as long as it keeps making progress, up to LLM_MAX_CALL (300 s). The proxy streams
text and reasoning token by token but holds back tool-call arguments until they are complete, so a request with
tools may stay silent after its last token for as long as its timeout above; one without tools may pause
LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT (15 s). LLM_HEDGE_AFTER sends a second copy of a call that has not started after that many
seconds and keeps whichever starts first (the losing copy may still be billed).
"""
import asyncio
import contextvars
import os
import time
from contextlib import AsyncExitStack

import httpx2
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelAPIError, ModelHTTPError
from pydantic_ai.messages import ModelMessage, ModelResponse
from pydantic_ai.models import ModelRequestParameters
from pydantic_ai.models.openai import OpenAIChatModel
from pydantic_ai.providers.openai import OpenAIProvider
from pydantic_ai.settings import ModelSettings

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 45.0  # thinking off: steps answer in seconds, so a hang shows early
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_THINKING = 90.0  # thinking on: a call reading a whole page may take 25 to 45 s
DEFAULT_RETRIES = 6
os.environ.setdefault("PYDANTIC_AI_NO_BANNER", "1")


def env_seconds(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    """A positive number from the environment, or `default` when unset, empty or unusable."""
    try:
        value = float(os.environ.get(name, "") or default)
    except ValueError:
        return default
    return value if value > 0 else default


def timeout_seconds(thinking: bool = False) -> float:
    """Seconds one model call may take before it is given up and retried: LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING for thinking-on
    calls (falling back to LLM_TIMEOUT when it is larger), LLM_TIMEOUT otherwise."""
    short = env_seconds("LLM_TIMEOUT", DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
    if not thinking:
        return short
    return max(short, env_seconds("LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING", DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_THINKING))


def retries() -> int:
    """How many times a failed or timed-out call is retried (LLM_RETRIES, default 6; 0 turns retries off)."""
    try:
        value = int(os.environ.get("LLM_RETRIES", "") or DEFAULT_RETRIES)
    except ValueError:
        return DEFAULT_RETRIES
    return value if value >= 0 else DEFAULT_RETRIES


DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN = 20.0  # measured: the first chunk came within 9.4 s (p90 5.9 s) in 179 calls, either mode
DEFAULT_IDLE = 15.0  # text and reasoning tokens arrive at most ~1.5 s apart while the model answers
DEFAULT_MAX_CALL = 300.0  # a streamed answer is not cut by the proxy: one runaway reasoning ran 814 s


def watchdog() -> bool:
    """Whether calls are streamed and judged by progress (LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1) instead of a whole-call deadline."""
    return os.environ.get("LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG", "").strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")


def hedge_seconds() -> float:
    """After how many seconds without a first chunk a second copy of the call is sent (LLM_HEDGE_AFTER; 0 = never)."""
    try:
        value = float(os.environ.get("LLM_HEDGE_AFTER", "") or 0)
    except ValueError:
        return 0.0
    return max(value, 0.0)


def _backoff(attempt: int) -> float:
    """Seconds to wait before retry `attempt`: 0.5 s doubling, capped at 8 s (as the OpenAI client does)."""
    return min(0.5 * 2 ** (attempt - 1), 8.0)


class Stalled(Exception):
    """A streamed call stopped making progress (raised by the watchdog, then retried)."""


# The progress limits of the call being made in this task; set by _WatchdogModel, read by the stream wrapper.
_WATCH: contextvars.ContextVar["_Limits | None"] = contextvars.ContextVar("llm_watch", default=None)


class _Limits:
    def __init__(self, *, first: float, idle: float, silence: float, tools: bool) -> None:
        self.first, self.idle, self.silence, self.tools = first, idle, silence, tools

    @property
    def quiet(self) -> float:
        """How long the call may go without a token once it has started: a request with tools may be writing tool
        arguments, which the proxy only sends when they are complete."""
        return max(self.idle, self.silence) if self.tools else self.idle


def _progress(chunk) -> bool:
    """Whether a stream chunk carries model output (text, reasoning or a tool call), not just a role or usage."""
    for choice in getattr(chunk, "choices", None) or ():
        delta = choice.delta
        if delta is None:
            continue
        extra = delta.model_extra or {}
        if delta.content or delta.tool_calls or extra.get("reasoning_content") or extra.get("reasoning"):
            return True

class _WatchedStream:
    """An OpenAI chunk stream that raises Stalled when the call goes quiet for longer than its limits allow.
    The proxy's keep-alive comments never reach here (the SSE decoder drops them), so they do not count."""

    def __init__(self, stream, limits: _Limits) -> None:
        self._stream, self._limits = stream, limits
        self._chunks = 0
        self._last = time.monotonic()

    def _wait(self) -> float:
        quiet = self._limits.first if not self._chunks else self._limits.quiet
        return max(self._last + quiet - time.monotonic(), 0.0)

    async def __aiter__(self):
        source = self._stream.__aiter__()
        while True:
            try:
                chunk = await asyncio.wait_for(anext(source), self._wait())
            except StopAsyncIteration:
                return
            except TimeoutError:
                if not self._chunks:
                    raise Stalled(f"no first chunk within {self._limits.first:g}s") from None
                raise Stalled(f"no progress for {self._limits.quiet:g}s after {self._chunks} chunks") from None
            if not self._chunks or _progress(chunk):
                self._last = time.monotonic()
            self._chunks += 1
            yield chunk

    async def __aenter__(self):
        await self._stream.__aenter__()
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc) -> None:
        await self._stream.__aexit__(*exc)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._stream.close()

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return getattr(self._stream, name)


class _WatchdogModel(OpenAIChatModel):
    """The OpenAI chat model; with LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG on, a request is streamed under progress limits, retried when
    it stalls, and handed back as one ModelResponse, so agents run unchanged."""

    async def _completions_create(self, messages, stream, model_settings, model_request_parameters):
        response = await super()._completions_create(messages, stream, model_settings, model_request_parameters)
        limits = _WATCH.get()
        if stream and limits is not None and not isinstance(response, ModelResponse):
            return _WatchedStream(response, limits)
        return response

    async def request(self, messages: list[ModelMessage], model_settings: ModelSettings | None,
                      model_request_parameters: ModelRequestParameters) -> ModelResponse:
        if not watchdog():
            return await super().request(messages, model_settings, model_request_parameters)
        settings = ModelSettings(**(model_settings or {}))
        thinking = bool(((settings.get("extra_body") or {}).get("chat_template_kwargs") or {}).get("enable_thinking"))
        silence = float(settings.get("timeout") or timeout_seconds(thinking))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        cap = env_seconds("LLM_MAX_CALL", DEFAULT_MAX_CALL)
        settings["timeout"] = cap  # the HTTP layer only guards the cap; progress is judged here
        tools = bool(model_request_parameters.function_tools or model_request_parameters.output_tools)
        limits = _Limits(first=env_seconds("LLM_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT", DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN),
                         idle=env_seconds("LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT", DEFAULT_IDLE), silence=silence, tools=tools)
        attempts = retries() + 1
        for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
            token = _WATCH.set(limits)
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(cap):
                    return await self._attempt(messages, settings, model_request_parameters, limits)
            except (Stalled, TimeoutError, httpx2.TransportError) as error:
                reason = str(error) or f"no answer within {cap:g}s"
            except ModelAPIError as error:
                if isinstance(error, ModelHTTPError) and error.status_code < 500 and error.status_code != 429:
                    raise
                reason = str(error)
            finally:
                _WATCH.reset(token)
            if attempt == attempts:
                raise ModelAPIError(self.model_name, f"model call failed {attempts} times; last: {reason}")
            print(f"[model] stalled thinking {'on' if thinking else 'off'}: {reason}; retry {attempt}/{attempts - 1}",
                  flush=True)
            await asyncio.sleep(_backoff(attempt))
        raise AssertionError("unreachable")

    async def _attempt(self, messages, settings, params, limits: _Limits) -> ModelResponse:
        """One streamed call (two when hedging): wait for the first chunk, then read the stream to its end."""
        async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
            streamed = await self._start(stack, messages, settings, params, limits)
            async for _ in streamed:
                pass
            return streamed.get()

    async def _open(self, messages, settings, params):
        stack = AsyncExitStack()
        try:
            streamed = await stack.enter_async_context(self.request_stream(messages, settings, params))
        except BaseException:
            await stack.aclose()
            raise
        return stack, streamed

    async def _start(self, stack: AsyncExitStack, messages, settings, params, limits: _Limits):
        """Open the stream (request_stream returns once the first chunk is in). With LLM_HEDGE_AFTER, a second copy
        goes out when the first has not started by then; the first copy to start wins, the other is dropped."""
        hedge = hedge_seconds()
        tasks = [asyncio.create_task(self._open(messages, settings, params))]
        first_copy = tasks[0]
        deadline = time.monotonic() + limits.first
        hedged = False
        try:
            if 0 < hedge < limits.first:
                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=hedge)
                if not done:
                    print(f"[model] no first chunk after {hedge:g}s: sending a hedge copy", flush=True)
                    tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._open(messages, settings, params)))
                    deadline = time.monotonic() + limits.first
                    hedged = True
            while tasks:
                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0),
                                             return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
                if not done:
                    raise Stalled(f"no first chunk within {limits.first:g}s")
                for task in done:
                    tasks.remove(task)
                    if task.exception() is None:
                        inner, streamed = task.result()
                        stack.push_async_callback(inner.aclose)
                        if hedged:
                            print(f"[model] hedge: the {'first' if task is first_copy else 'hedge'} copy "
                                  "started first and is kept", flush=True)
                        return streamed
                    if not tasks:
                        raise task.exception()  # type: ignore[misc]
            raise AssertionError("unreachable")
        finally:
            for task in tasks:  # copies that lost the race or never started
                task.cancel()
            for result in await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True):
                if isinstance(result, tuple):
                    await result[0].aclose()


def _thinking(request: httpx2.Request) -> str:
    content = request.content or b""
    return "on" if b'"enable_thinking": true' in content or b'"enable_thinking":true' in content else "off"


async def _sent(request: httpx2.Request) -> None:
    """Note when a call left; a retry (the OpenAI client counts them in a header) is logged, with the timeout the
    attempt runs under, so a hanging model shows in the run logs before the worker times out."""
    request.extensions["sent_at"] = time.monotonic()
    attempt = int(request.headers.get("x-stainless-retry-count", "0") or 0)
    if attempt:
        print(f"[model] retry {attempt}/{retries()} thinking {_thinking(request)} "
              f"timeout {request.headers.get('x-stainless-read-timeout', '?')}s", flush=True)


class _TimedBody(httpx2.AsyncByteStream):
    """A response body that logs the call once it has fully arrived: the proxy sends the headers early and a
    thinking-on body can follow much later, so logging at the headers would hide the real duration."""

    def __init__(self, response: httpx2.Response) -> None:
        self._response = response
        self._stream = response.stream

    @property
    def elapsed(self):
        return getattr(self._stream, "elapsed", None)

    async def __aiter__(self):
        complete = False
        try:
            async for chunk in self._stream:  # type: ignore[union-attr]
                complete = complete or b"data: [DONE]" in chunk  # a stream's reader may stop right there
                yield chunk
            complete = True
        finally:
            _log(self._response, complete)

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        await self._stream.aclose()  # type: ignore[union-attr]


def _log(response: httpx2.Response, complete: bool) -> None:
    """One line per model call: status, seconds until the body was in (and until the headers came), request
    size, thinking mode, and which retry it was."""
    request = response.request
    now = time.monotonic()
    sent, headers = request.extensions.get("sent_at", now), request.extensions.get("headers_at", now)
    attempt = request.headers.get("x-stainless-retry-count", "0")
    print(f"[model] {response.status_code} {now - sent:.1f}s (headers {headers - sent:.1f}s) "
          f"{len(request.content or b'')} bytes thinking {_thinking(request)}"
          + (f" retry {attempt}" if attempt not in ("", "0") else "") + ("" if complete else " incomplete"),
          flush=True)


async def _answered(response: httpx2.Response) -> None:
    """Called when the headers are in: remember when, and log the call once the body has been read."""
    response.request.extensions["headers_at"] = time.monotonic()
    response.stream = _TimedBody(response)


class _DeadlineClient(httpx2.AsyncClient):
    """An HTTP client whose read timeout is a deadline for the whole call (headers and body), so the proxy's
    keep-alive newlines cannot hold a call open past it. Expiry raises ReadTimeout, which the OpenAI client retries."""

    async def send(self, request: httpx2.Request, *, stream: bool = False, **kwargs) -> httpx2.Response:
        seconds = (request.extensions.get("timeout") or {}).get("read")
        if not seconds:
            return await super().send(request, stream=stream, **kwargs)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
        try:
            response = await asyncio.wait_for(super().send(request, stream=True, **kwargs), seconds)
        except TimeoutError:
            raise httpx2.ReadTimeout(f"no answer within {seconds:g}s", request=request) from None
        if stream:
            return response
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(response.aread(), max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.001))
        except TimeoutError:
            await response.aclose()
            raise httpx2.ReadTimeout(f"no complete answer within {seconds:g}s", request=request) from None
        except BaseException:
            await response.aclose()
            raise
        return response


def model() -> OpenAIChatModel:
    """The worker model. The client's own timeout is the thinking-off one; `settings()` overrides it per request,
    so a thinking-on agent gets its longer timeout without a client of its own. With LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG on, the
    model streams each call and judges it by progress instead (`_WatchdogModel`)."""
    client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
                         timeout=timeout_seconds(thinking=False), max_retries=retries(),
                         http_client=_DeadlineClient(event_hooks={"request": [_sent], "response": [_answered]}))

"""A run's trace: one JSON line per event in a file, and a short line on stdout for the run logs."""
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path


CURRENT: "Trace | None" = None  # the run's trace, for the summary at the very end


def print_summary() -> None:
    """The current run's phase and failure events in one block (no-op before a trace exists)."""
    if CURRENT is not None:
        CURRENT.summary()


class Trace:
    def __init__(self, directory: str | None = None):
        global CURRENT
        CURRENT = self
        self.key: list[str] = []
        self.started = self.last = time.monotonic()
        directory = directory or os.environ.get("TRACE_DIR", "traces")
        Path(directory).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.path = Path(directory) / time.strftime("run-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S.jsonl")
        self.file = self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8")

    # events that mark a phase or a failure; repeated in one block at the end of the run (summary())
    KEY_KINDS = {"start", "done", "stopped", "problem", "start_failed", "spec_done", "tender_facts", "mail_kind",
                 "answer", "summary_check", "last_chance", "crashed", "decision_disputed", "helper_error"}

    def event(self, worker: str, kind: str, quiet: bool = False, **data) -> None:
        self.last = time.monotonic()
        seconds = round(self.last - self.started, 2)
        self.file.write(json.dumps({"t": seconds, "worker": worker, "kind": kind, **data}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        self.file.flush()
        if quiet:  # file only, e.g. the full page views
            return
        brief = " ".join(f"{k}={str(v)[:120]!r}" if isinstance(v, str) else f"{k}={v}" for k, v in data.items())
        print(f"[{seconds:7.1f}s] {worker:<15} {kind:<12} {brief}", flush=True)
        if kind in self.KEY_KINDS:
            self.key.append(f"[{seconds:7.1f}s] {worker:<15} {kind:<12} {brief[:150]}")

    def summary(self, limit: int = 120) -> None:
        """Print the phase and failure events again in one block: the platform keeps only the last few hundred
        lines of a run's output, so without this the early phases are missing from every run log."""
        lines = self.key if len(self.key) <= limit else self.key[:20] + ["  ..."] + self.key[-(limit - 21):]
        print("===== run summary =====\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n===== end of run summary =====", flush=True)

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5.5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` - it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events. When a streaming request defines user-defined (client) tools, set `eager_input_streaming: true` on each of those tools so large tool inputs (file contents, code, documents) stream as they are generated instead of arriving in one burst after the server finishes buffering them; the client then owns validation: the SDKs' tolerant parsers can return a silently truncated input instead of raising, so validate each parsed tool input against its schema before running it (the typed runner helpers such as `betaZodTool` / typed `@beta_tool` do this; `betaTool()` JSON-Schema tools and manual loops must validate themselves), treat a failure like invalid JSON (`INVALID_JSON` error `tool_result` when you hold the block, re-issue otherwise), check `max_tokens` / `refusal` stop reasons before running tools, and catch only the SDK's JSON error, never its typed API errors - pattern in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` -> Eager input streaming. Leave it off for non-streaming requests, for server tools, and when the request goes through a proxy or an older Bedrock model deployment that rejects the field.

## Warning: API Drift - Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025-2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing - the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5/5.1 / Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.5 / 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5.5/5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6.
